words.root_gloss_range: praise, commendation, recognition of praiseworthiness, and grateful response; remote idiomatic branches are not locally active
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْحَمْدُ}} ({{tr:al-ḥamdu}}) opens the ayah as a definite nominal topic, so praise is presented as an established reality assigned onward rather than as an explicit speaker saying, "I praise." The {{ar:ح م د}} ({{tr:ḥ-m-d}}) range keeps praise thicker than thanks alone: it includes recognition of worth, gratitude for benefit, and commendation of intrinsic excellence, while the local form does not activate every remote root branch. Its first-word position makes praise the discourse launch after the basmala, and the following predicate relation directs the whole praise field to Allah before the clause widens into lordship over the worlds. The phrase also joins recurring praise-to-God openings and closures (6:1, 18:1, 34:1, 35:1), while 1:7 later names the benefaction that makes praise and thanks intelligible.

topics.headline: definite nominal praise stands before the genitive chain
topics.summary: The standard nominative definite noun makes praise the clause topic; case and form variants expose other possible parses but do not replace the local nominal predication.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that praise is not narrated as a timed act by a visible speaker but set down as the stable topic of the whole clause.
topics.reason: Local syntax forces a nominal clause with the following prepositional phrase as predicate, while variant evidence only shows how a different case would alter the frame.

topics.headline: praise includes recognition, gratitude, and commendation
topics.summary: The root-family rows distinguish this praise noun from narrower thanks and from broader praise of any kind, while local syntax keeps the concise noun as the active form.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the opening word carries gratitude and recognition of worth together, not merely a generic word for thanks.
topics.reason: V4 supports praise and praiseworthiness as central branches, but the local gerund does not license every derivative or idiomatic branch as an active sense.

topics.headline: praise joins a recurring deity-lordship-worlds cluster
topics.summary: The praise noun is distributionally tied to the divine name and then expanded locally by the lordship and worlds terms; the cross-surah praise formula is concretely visible at 6:1, 18:1, 34:1, and 35:1.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first word is already positioned inside a recurring Quranic praise-to-God formula that this ayah immediately expands.
topics.reason: The local construction and supplied collocation data both support a praise-to-Allah relation, with the phrase joining known praise openings and closures.

topics.headline: the opening stance moves from invocation to praise
topics.summary: After the basmala, the ayah begins with praise rather than an explicit human actor; the same surah later grounds the response in divine benefaction at 1:7.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the surah's first full declaration begins with praise as stance before it explains causes, requests, or human agency.
topics.reason: The opening position, suppressed speaker, boundary shift from 1:1, and audible nominative ending all reinforce the word as discourse launch rather than a passing noun.

words.gloss_range: prepositional governor assigning the praise relation to the following divine name as belonging, due-ness, and restriction
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li-}}) is small but controls the clause's assignment of praise. It governs the following name and makes the praise field belong to, be due to, and be restricted to Allah without adding a separate emphatic word. Because it is bound into the recited phrase with the name, the relation is heard as attachment as well as parsed as governance. It also marks the boundary shift from beginning by the divine name in 1:1 to assigning praise to the named referent here.

topics.headline: the particle assigns praise as belonging and due
topics.summary: The particle keeps possession, entitlement, and restriction live together, so praise is not free-floating or transferable to rival recipients.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the relationship between praise and Allah is carried by a governor that means more than a bare destination marker.
topics.reason: The bundle forces the particle as a genitive-governing preposition and preserves the semantic load of belonging, due-ness, and restriction.

topics.headline: bound form makes the dependency audible
topics.summary: The proclitic particle attaches to the divine name, so the syntactic dependency appears in the visible and audible shape of the phrase.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the particle-name bond is not only grammatical but also part of the recited form.
topics.reason: The surface attaches the preposition to its complement, matching the syntactically forced governance relation.

topics.headline: preposition shift turns invocation into attribution
topics.summary: The boundary moves from the instrumental preposition of 1:1 to this assignment particle, changing the mode from beginning an act to assigning praise.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a precise grammatical turn between 1:1 and 1:2: invocation becomes attribution.
topics.reason: The source row gives the concrete 1:1 boundary contrast, and nothing in the local syntax blocks it.

topics.headline: grammar, form, and restriction converge
topics.summary: The particle simultaneously governs case, fuses to its complement, and restricts the praise relation.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices why this one-letter particle bears a major hinge function in the clause.
topics.reason: The synthesis row is preserved because it combines distinct validated mechanisms rather than adding decorative repetition.

words.gloss_range: the fixed divine proper name as governed praise-recipient, then anchor for appositional expansion
words.root_gloss_range: deity, worship, turning toward, and disputed derivational pressure; locally fixed as the unique divine name rather than a generic class noun
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:allāhi}}) is governed by the preceding particle, so the divine name is the recipient and rightful holder of praise, not a new subject competing with the opening praise noun. The {{ar:أ ل ه}} ({{tr:ʾ-l-h}}) background keeps worship, turning toward, and the disputed sense of overwhelming refuge in view, while the local surface remains the fixed proper name. Its recurrence from 1:1 re-anchors the same divine name in a changed frame: first invoked, now assigned all praise, and then expanded by the following lordship title into final cosmic scope. The name becomes the node tying praise, title, and worlds together. Even the vowel-harmony variant affects the transition's sound rather than the referent.

topics.headline: genitive governance makes the name praise-recipient
topics.summary: The divine name is governed by the particle as a genitive complement; variant evidence shows other possible frames but the local reading keeps attribution rather than an explicit performed verb.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Allah is grammatically the endpoint of praise while praise remains the clause's subject.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence forces the prepositional relation, while the verbal variant is only contrastive and does not govern the canonical parse.

topics.headline: proper name carries worship and refuge pressure
topics.summary: The word is a fixed divine proper name, but the derivational dispute keeps worship, turning toward, and overwhelming refuge as semantic pressure around the praise relation.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the praise-recipient is not a generic deity term but the unique named referent toward whom worship and refuge converge.
topics.reason: The local form is the proper name, so the disputed derivations are retained as pressure and provenance rather than treated as separate local lexical senses.

topics.headline: the repeated name pivots into appositional expansion
topics.summary: The name recurs from 1:1, now governed by the praise particle, and then becomes the anchor for the following appositional title.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same divine name binds 1:1 and 1:2 while the grammar around it changes from invocation to praise-attribution.
topics.reason: The local apposition and same-surah recurrence support the word as hinge between compact praise and the subsequent expansion.

topics.headline: variant smooths sound without changing referent
topics.summary: The vowel-harmony reading exposes acoustic smoothing between the praise noun and divine name, but it preserves the same governed referent.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that recitational sound can tighten the praise-name link without changing the grammar or referent.
topics.reason: The accepted variant affects phonetic transition only; the bundle does not license semantic substitution.

topics.headline: divine name joins praise, lordship, and worlds
topics.summary: The supplied cooccurrence rows place the divine name in a dense field with praise, lordship, and worlds, and the local ayah instantiates that cluster.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the name is the central node holding the ayah's praise, title, and cosmic scope together.
topics.reason: The row family is not merely statistical background because every named relation is locally present in the clause.

words.gloss_range: genitive appositional title and construct head: Lord, owner, master, nurturer, and sustainer in relation to the worlds
words.root_gloss_range: owning, mastering, governing, raising, fostering, managing, and forming; unrelated homonymic branches such as syrup, cloud, pact, or particle uses are not locally active
words.prose: {{ar:رَبِّ}} ({{tr:rabbi}}) turns the praised name into a relational title: the referent is not only named but specified as Lord of the final scope. Grammatically it stays genitive as apposition to the divine name and as construct head over the worlds term, so the ayah widens without starting a new clause. The {{ar:ر ب ب}} ({{tr:r-b-b}}) range keeps ownership, mastery, governing care, and staged nurturing together; the word does not reduce to static sovereignty. Its compact doubled form and dominant noun pattern make lordship a stable office. The title carries mercy language from 1:1 into enacted care and is immediately colored by the mercy descriptions of 1:3, while the ownership title in 1:4 shifts from cosmic nurture to judgmental mastery.

topics.headline: apposition binds the name to cosmic scope
topics.summary: The word is genitive in apposition to the divine name and construct head over the final worlds term; case variants expose alternatives but the standard reading keeps the binding intact.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah expands by apposition and construct binding, not by launching a second verbal statement.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence licenses both the apposition to the divine name and the construct relation to the final word; variant parses remain contrastive.

topics.headline: lordship is ownership plus formation and care
topics.summary: The root-family rows keep owning, mastering, governing, raising, fostering, formation, and devotional cultivation together, while unrelated root branches are not active locally.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the title makes divine authority developmental and caring as well as possessive.
topics.reason: V4 supports owner-master and tending-formation branches near the title, but the local divine construct excludes unrelated homonymic branches.

topics.headline: geminate noun compresses role into a title
topics.summary: The word appears as a concrete noun from a doubled root, with noun use dominant in distribution; the sound and form make the role compact and stable.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that nurturing and ruling are presented as a settled office rather than a single narrated act.
topics.reason: The local word is nominal, and the supplied distribution supports the noun-title pattern over a verbal nurturing event.

topics.headline: lordship widens praise and anticipates later titles
topics.summary: The title links the divine name, praise, and worlds in a recurring cluster, bridges mercy from 1:1 and 1:3, and anticipates the ownership title of 1:4.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this word is the hinge by which praise to Allah becomes a cosmic claim and prepares the surah's next divine descriptions.
topics.reason: The local word joins all three neighboring terms and the supplied inter-ayah rows give concrete same-surah links at 1:1, 1:3, and 1:4.

topics.headline: grammar, polysemy, variants, and sound converge
topics.summary: The synthesis row is retained because apposition, nurturer-master-owner range, case pressure, and doubled sound each explain part of the word's expansion work.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices why this single title carries much of the ayah's widening from praise-recipient to Lord of worlds.
topics.reason: The convergence is not reducible to one row family; all named components survive after guardrail checks.

words.gloss_range: the genitive plural worlds/communities governed by the preceding lordship title; scope is many knowable, sign-bearing orders rather than one inert realm
words.root_gloss_range: knowing, teaching, marking, distinguishing, and created realms as knowable/sign-bearing orders; unrelated branches such as cleftness, water, or animal names are not locally active
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ}} ({{tr:al-ʿālamīn}}) lands the ayah on its widest scope. As the genitive dependent of the preceding title, it names the domains owned, governed, and nurtured by that lordship. The plural form prevents a single flat world from being heard; it distributes the relation across many communities or orders. The {{ar:ع ل م}} ({{tr:ʿ-l-m}}) background makes those worlds legible and knowable, even sign-bearing, while the local noun does not become a generic word for knowledge itself. Its final position completes the movement from praise, to Allah, to Lord, to all worlds, and the phrase joins repeated praise-lordship formulas (6:45, 10:10, 37:182, 39:75, 40:65, 45:36). Its ending also joins the opening surah's sound pattern that continues in 1:3 and 1:4.

topics.headline: genitive plural is the governed domain of lordship
topics.summary: The word is the second term of the construct, so the worlds are the domain and object of the preceding lordship relation.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word is not an added setting but the governed scope of the title before it.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence syntactically forces the word as the genitive dependent of the title.

topics.headline: plural form distributes lordship across many domains
topics.summary: The plural shape and rational-plural pressure prevent a single undifferentiated realm and point toward many communities or ordered domains.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine lordship is distributed across many ordered communities rather than one flat cosmic container.
topics.reason: The local grammar confirms a genitive plural, and the CRITICAL rows' rational-plural claim is not contradicted by the guardrails.

topics.headline: worlds are knowable and sign-bearing orders
topics.summary: The root-family rows tie the worlds term to knowing, teaching, marking, and signs; locally this enriches the worlds as knowable orders, not as an active knowledge verb.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final scope is not inert space but ordered reality that can be known, marked, and distinguished.
topics.reason: V4 includes knowledge, marking, and world/created-realm branches; the local noun selects the worlds branch while preserving epistemic pressure.

topics.headline: final totality completes the praise-lordship formula
topics.summary: The word completes the local movement from praise to divine name to lordship to worlds, and the phrase joins formulaic settings at 6:45, 10:10, 37:182, 39:75, 40:65, and 45:36.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah's last word retroactively expands the whole clause to universal scope and joins a repeated Quranic formula.
topics.reason: The local final position and supplied cross-surah references support a formulaic and climactic closing function.

topics.headline: sound pressure marks the ayah ending
topics.summary: The hamza-insertion variant is phonetic rather than semantic, and the final ending links the word to the near closures of 1:3 and 1:4.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word carries closure through sound as well as through scope.
topics.reason: The variant and cadence rows are retained as phonetic payoff, while the local referent remains the plural worlds.

topics.headline: invocation widens into knowable domains
topics.summary: The boundary moves from private invocation in 1:1 to a cosmological declaration, with naming and knowing linked through the final worlds term.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the opening movement broadens from named invocation to the total field of governed, knowable domains.
topics.reason: The boundary and synthesis rows preserve distinct payoffs: scene widening, epistemic linkage, plural scope, closure, and cadence.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Praise as an evaluative verdict after testing the order.** Lexical evidence: ح م د B001, praise opposite blame; ح م د B002, finding something satisfactory after testing; ع ل م B001, knowing as clarity. Structural cue: praise follows the named mercy and precedes the list of lordship, judgment, worship, and guidance. Assigned role: الحمد is both spoken praise and a judgment that the whole disclosed order proves praiseworthy. Abductive move: the packet gives praise/testing/clarity; I infer that the following ayat function as the evidentiary field that makes praise intelligible. Reading change: “all praise” reads less like a formula and more like the verdict produced by seeing the whole mechanism.

2. **Lordship as stage-by-stage cultivation of worlds.** Lexical evidence: ر ب ب B001, lordship/ownership/authority; ر ب ب B002, repair, nurture, completion; ع ل م B002, distinguishing signs and road markers. Structural cue: “Lord” is attached to “worlds,” while later 1:6 asks for a road and 1:7 identifies the path by people marked by favor. Assigned role: رب is the maintainer who forms worlds into legible, navigable fields. Abductive move: the packet supplies nurture and markers; I infer that the worlds are not merely objects owned but terrains cultivated into guidance-bearing order. Reading change: “Lord of the worlds” reads as “caretaker and completer of sign-marked realms.”

3. **The worlds as signs, not only domains.** Lexical evidence: ع ل م B002, a distinguishing mark that points to something; ه د ي B001 in 1:6, guidance to road/truth; ص ر ط B001 in 1:6–1:7, road. Structural cue: عَٰلَمِينَ sits immediately after رب and later the path request asks for orientation. Assigned role: worlds act as marked surfaces through which lordship becomes knowable and directional. Abductive move: the packet supplies “worlds” through the root علم and “path/guidance” later; I infer that visibility of marks enables movement. Reading change: the ayah’s cosmology becomes semiotic: the worlds are readable signs under رب, not inert scenery.

4. **Praise resists benefaction-credit rivalry.** Lexical evidence: ح م د B005, claiming praise by favor; ن ع م B001 in 1:7, bestowed favor; ء ل ه B001, worshipped object. Structural cue: 1:7 mentions favor bestowed by “You,” while 1:5 confines worship and help to “You.” Assigned role: الحمد prevents favor from becoming a human credit-claim. Abductive move: the packet supplies favor and exclusive address; I infer that all benefaction-credit is redirected to Allah. Reading change: praise is not only gratitude; it blocks rival ownership of benefaction.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 1:7 sharpened رب العالمين: “favored,” “angered,” and “astray” showed that the worlds are not abstract cosmic plurality but a morally sorted field. The animal/stray branch of ض ل ل B005 also made رب sound unexpectedly like owner-care: the Lord of worlds contrasts with ownerless wandering.
reader_a.turkish_prose_synthesis_md: Hamd, yalnızca övgü sözü değil, görülen düzenin denenip övülmeye layık bulunmasıdır. “Âlemlerin Rabbi” ifadesinde Rab, sadece sahip ve hükümran değil, âlemleri aşama aşama yetiştiren, onaran ve tamamlayan bakıcıdır. Âlemler de işaretsiz boş alanlar değil, yolu gösteren alametlerle dolu okunabilir sahalardır. Son ayetteki nimet, gazap ve dalalet ayrımı bu hamdi ahlaki olarak sınıflanmış bir dünya içinde duyulur kılar.

reader_b.activated_readings_md:
1. **Praise as tested recognition, not only spontaneous acclaim.** Evidence: `ح م د B001` praise/thanksgiving, `ح م د B002` finding something praiseworthy after testing, `ن ع م B001` favor in 1:7, and `غ ض ب B001`/`ض ل ل B001` negative alternatives in 1:7. Mechanism: the later contrast between favored, angered, and lost paths makes الحمد sound like a verdict reached after discriminating between outcomes. The packet supplies praise, favor, anger, and straying; I infer the evaluative testing relation. Abductive move: praise becomes meaningful when the path has alternatives that could have ended in anger or loss. Reading change: “الحمد” reads as thankful recognition after moral-path testing, not only as opening doxology.

2. **Rabb as caretaker who brings many marked worlds to completion.** Evidence: `ر ب ب B002` repair, nurture, and completion; `ع ل م B002` distinguishing mark/landmark; `ه د ي B001` guidance toward way/truth in 1:6; `ق و م B009` support/mainstay in 1:6. Mechanism: “العالمين” is activated by the branch of signs and markers: worlds are readable, marked domains that require ربّ care, and guidance later asks to move through those marks rightly. The packet supplies Rabb, worlds/knowledge-sign branches, guidance, and straightness; I infer that nurture makes the marked order navigable. Abductive move: a ربّ of many worlds is not only owner of plurality but the one who maintains their intelligibility. Reading change: “رب العالمين” becomes a claim about sustaining a legible cosmos, not only possessing all beings.

3. **Lordship as authority, covenant, and administered dependence.** Evidence: `ر ب ب B001` lordship/ownership/authority, `ر ب ب B011` covenant or protection pact, `م ل ك B003` kingship/dominion and `د ي ن B001/B002` obedience/reckoning in 1:4, plus `ع ب د B003` worship in 1:5. Mechanism: later obedience, judgment, and worship activate the legal-political side of ربّ: praise is directed to one whose care is also binding authority. The packet supplies authority, covenant, obedience, and worship; I infer that praise acknowledges administered dependence. Abductive move: if the speaker will later declare exclusive service, the ربّ here must already be more than a nurturer; he is the binding governor of the relation. Reading change: the ayah preserves both care and rule, rather than disambiguating Rabb into either tenderness or sovereignty.
reader_b.retrospective_surprises_md: 1:6 unexpectedly made `ع ل م B002` important: “worlds” began to look like marked terrain whose signs need guidance, not just a plural totality. 1:7 then fed back into الحمد through `ن ع م B001`; praise became gratitude for favor and also a recognition that some outcomes are not praiseworthy because they end in anger or loss.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A dependent community turns toward a sovereign divine addressee through worship, service, obedience, and petition.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The devotional relation extends lexically from willing worship into ownership and coercive service, while lordship also carries the countervailing function of nurture.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Worship and Obedient Submission
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Worshippers direct humble obedience to the one recognized as deity and organizing religious authority.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: worship as an act `ء ل ه:B001/m01`; the worshipped deity `ء ل ه:B001/m02`; obedient religious submission `د ي ن:B001/m01`; humble worship and service `ع ب د:B003/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The scene joins the divine object of worship to the human act of worship, then specifies the relation as obedience enacted with humility. Religion is active here as an ordering relation rather than merely a named doctrine.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A dependent community turns toward a sovereign divine addressee through worship, service, obedience, and petition.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The devotional relation extends lexically from willing worship into ownership and coercive service, while lordship also carries the countervailing function of nurture.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Sovereignty, Ownership, and Service
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A lord and king possesses a domain, governs it, and stands over dependents whose service ranges from honored attendance to enslavement.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: divine lordship `ر ب ب:B001/m01`; proprietary mastery `ر ب ب:B001/m02`; kingship and sovereignty `م ل ك:B003/m01`; ownership and disposal of property `م ل ك:B002/m01`; the enslaved dependent `ع ب د:B001/m01`; coercive dominion `د ي ن:B004/m01`; the honored or venerated servant `ع ب د:B006/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Lordship and kingship supply the governing agent, ownership supplies the legal relation to a domain, and servitude supplies the dependent role. The honored servant and the enslaved subject expose opposite social realizations of the same vertical relation.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Good is conferred through compassion and maintenance, stabilized as welfare, and answered by praise or recognition.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Tenderness expands into practical provisioning, repair, guardianship, and structural support, while praise can function either as gratitude or as a claim imposed by a patron.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Compassionate Provision and Nurture
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A caregiver feels tenderness, nurtures a dependent over time, guards its affairs, and supplies or repairs what sustains a good condition.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: tenderness and compassion `ر ح م:B001/m01`; beneficent mercy `ر ح م:B001/m02`; conferred blessing `ن ع م:B001/m02`; good condition `ن ع م:B001/m01`; progressive nurture `ر ب ب:B002/m02`; guardianship and care `ق و م:B004/m01`; provision for dependents `غ ي ر:B001/m01`; repair of their equipment `غ ي ر:B001/m03`; practical aid `ع و ن:B001/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Compassion is the motive, progressive nurture and guardianship are the continuing operations, and food, equipment, and assistance are the practical means. Blessing names the resulting condition of the cared-for dependent.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Good is conferred through compassion and maintenance, stabilized as welfare, and answered by praise or recognition.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Tenderness expands into practical provisioning, repair, guardianship, and structural support, while praise can function either as gratitude or as a claim imposed by a patron.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Patronage, Support, and Claimed Recognition
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A patron supplies aid and the mainstay of another's life, then may present that support as a favor deserving praise.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: aid and mutual support `ع و ن:B001/m01`; the mainstay of an affair `م ل ك:B005/m01`; structural and livelihood support `ق و م:B009/m01`; benefaction or favor `ن ع م:B001/m02`; blessing as a conferred good `ر ب ب:B016/m03`; seeking praise for a favor `ح م د:B005/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Aid, mainstay, and livelihood form one support mechanism. The social relation becomes patronage when the giver converts that material dependence into a demand for acknowledgment.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Good is conferred through compassion and maintenance, stabilized as welfare, and answered by praise or recognition.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Knowing and Articulating the Praiseworthy
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Knowledge discerns a benefit or admirable quality and renders that recognition as praise, approval, or an honored name.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: praise and thanks `ح م د:B001/m01`; knowledge and recognition `ع ل م:B001/m01`; learned cultivation of knowledge `ر ب ب:B003/m01`; a person marked by many praised qualities `ح م د:B003/m01`; verbal approval `ن ع م:B003/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 1:2 `ٱلْحَمْدُ`, `رَبِّ`, and `ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ` (`ح م د`, `ر ب ب`, `ع ل م`); 1:7 `أَنْعَمْتَ` (`ن ع م`)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Knowledge supplies discriminating recognition, learned cultivation stabilizes that judgment, and praise gives it public form. The result can attach either to an act of benefaction or to a person whose qualities make the praise durable.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Naming, Invocation, and Direct Address
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A speaker identifies the addressee by name and turns that name into invocation, oath, or direct appeal.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: name and naming `س م و:B005/m01`; a namesake or comparable bearer of a name `س م و:B005/m02`; the divine name `ء ل ه:B002/m01`; oath and vocative formulas using that name `ء ل ه:B002/m02`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Naming establishes reference, while oath and vocative use convert reference into an active relation between speaker and addressee. The namesake motif defines identity comparatively by asking who else can bear the same designation.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Assent, Certification, and Qualification
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: An utterance confirms a claim, delegates judgment, or narrows it through difference, exception, negation, and approximation.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: affirmative response `ن ع م:B004/m01`; certification or delegated judgment `د ي ن:B007/m01`; otherness and difference `غ ي ر:B005/m01`; exception and negation `غ ي ر:B005/m02`; the approximating or quantifying particle `ر ب ب:B015/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Assent commits the speaker, certification authorizes another's word or judgment, and qualification sets the limits of the commitment. Approximation and exception show that discourse governs not only truth but also scope.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Reputation and Poetic Exchange
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Public speech circulates praise or blame until it becomes a person's audible reputation and social eminence.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: good reputation or public voice `س م و:B008/m01`; social eminence `س م و:B001/m02`; exchanged praise or satire in verse `ه د ي:B011/m01`; the person of many praised qualities `ح م د:B003/m01`; soliciting praise for favors `ح م د:B005/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Poetic exchange is the transmitting action, praise and satire supply opposite evaluations, and public voice is the resulting social state. Eminence describes the vertical effect of a reputation that others cannot easily match.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: The Reputed Captain's Ceremonial Bearing
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A maritime captain appears as a composed, publicly reputed leader whose station is marked by ceremonial scent.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: captain or chief of sailors `ر ب ب:B017/m01`; perfume brazier `ع ب د:B012/m01`; calm and dignified bearing `ه د ي:B010/m01`; good public reputation `س م و:B008/m01`; an elevated visible figure `س م و:B002/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The captain supplies the leading role, calm bearing and visibility make that role perceptible, reputation carries it beyond the immediate crew, and the perfume brazier gives the scene a ceremonial object of status.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The straight-road scene expands into landmarks, centerlines, and leading animals, while swallowing, mounting, cutting, and burial supply a shape-motion analogy for passage into disappearance.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: The Marked and Straight Route
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A traveler receives guidance, reads landmarks, enters the center of a prepared road, and maintains a straight course that can also become an established manner of conduct.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: gentle route guidance `ه د ي:B001/m01`; direction and manner `ه د ي:B002/m01`; road or straight path `ص ر ط:B001/m01`; straightness and rectitude `ق و م:B008/m01`; route landmark and boundary `ع ل م:B002/m02`; middle of the road or valley `م ل ك:B006/m01`; paved or trodden road `ع ب د:B005/m01`; established custom or habitual course `د ي ن:B005/m01`

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Guidance initiates movement, landmarks and boundaries make the route legible, a prepared surface and centerline stabilize traversal, and straightness describes its successful geometry. channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: The Visible Leader at the Front

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Visibility allows the leader to be tracked, the foremost position supplies direction, and the gathered animals supply the following participants. Leadership is thus rendered as a spatial relation before it becomes a social one.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Daylight, Zenith, and Celestial Marking
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A daylight span is located by the sun at zenith and by visible signs in the overhead sky.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: bounded daylight `ي و م:B001/m01`; the sun standing at midday `ق و م:B017/m01`; the overhead sky `س م و:B004/m01`; a lunar station `ن ع م:B007/m04`; a distinguishing sign `ع ل م:B002/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Daylight supplies the bounded interval, zenith gives it an internal midpoint, and sky signs provide a larger celestial coordinate system. Time is read through the positions of bodies that appear to stand overhead.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Duration, Pace, and Praised Attainment
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: An actor inhabits a duration, varies between delay and haste, intensifies effort, and reaches a praiseworthy limit without losing composure.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: an open duration of time `ي و م:B002/m01`; brief delay `ع ب د:B009/m01`; quick running `ع ب د:B009/m02`; increase or intensification `ن ع م:B010/m01`; the utmost praised goal `ح م د:B004/m01`; calm bearing `ه د ي:B010/m01`; continued residence `ر ب ب:B007/m01`

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Consecrated Offering

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Livestock supplies the transferable material, consecration fixes its destination, and worship supplies the relation that distinguishes an offering from an ordinary gift.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Kinship, Fosterage, and Continuing Care
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A child belongs to a network of blood and acquired kin whose caregiver assumes responsibility for nurture and continuity.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: close kinship `ر ح م:B002/m01`; maintaining kin ties `ر ح م:B002/m02`; stepchild `ر ب ب:B005/m01`; foster caregiver `ر ب ب:B005/m02`; progressive child-rearing `ر ب ب:B002/m02`; guardianship `ق و م:B004/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Blood relation supplies one form of belonging, fosterage supplies another, and guardianship turns both into continuing obligations. Progressive nurture is the operation that converts formal relation into lived care.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A named outsider or dependent receives protected standing through covenant, certification, and a rule of compensatory redress.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Species and age make animals classifiable, gathering makes them a herd, and the lead animal provides internal order. The stray defines the boundary case where an animal loses both group placement and known ownership.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: Habitation, Water, and the Living Landscape
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Habitation becomes viable when authority, residence, water, weather, and vegetation converge into a sustaining place.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The field moves from a city defined by obedience into a camp secured by stored water, then upward to layered clouds, persistent rain, gentle wind, and enduring plants.
